    Chick mortality as a result of adults not attending the nest

    calc_unattendmortality.Rd

    Determines whether a chick dies as a result of being left unattended by its parents during a model time step. Longer periods of unattendance increase the risk of mortality through mechanisms such as predation or exposure.

    The probability of death increases linearly with the duration of unattendance, reaching 100% when the unattendance period equals or exceeds the species-specific critical threshold.

    A stochastic draw is then used to determine whether mortality occurs.

    Usage

    calc_unattendmortality(CoD, alive, unattend_hrs, max_hrs)

    Arguments

    CoD

    Current cause of death. Typically "none" if the chick is alive.

    alive

    Indicator of whether the chick is currently alive (1) or dead (0).

    unattend_hrs

    Number of hours for which the chick was left unattended.

    max_hrs

    Species-specific critical unattendance threshold (hours), above which mortality is assumed to occur.

    Value

    A character string giving the updated cause of death. Returns the original value of CoD if the chick survives.

    Details

    The probability of mortality is calculated as:

    $$P(death) = unattend\_hrs / max\_hrs$$

    capped at a maximum value of 1.

    Mortality is then determined through a binomial random draw. If mortality occurs, the cause of death is updated to "unattended".

    See also

    calc_chickcare()

    Examples

    # Chick attended by its parents
calc_unattendmortality(
  CoD = "none",
  alive = 1,
  unattend_hrs = 0,
  max_hrs = 18
)
#> [1] "none"

# Chick left unattended for a short period
calc_unattendmortality(
  CoD = "none",
  alive = 1,
  unattend_hrs = 6,
  max_hrs = 18
)
#> [1] "none"

# Chick left unattended for the maximum allowable time
calc_unattendmortality(
  CoD = "none",
  alive = 1,
  unattend_hrs = 18,
  max_hrs = 18
)
#> [1] "unattended"
